The ordered chain blocker_moved -> (has_door_key & blocker_moved) -> door_open -> target_picked_up matches the only feasible constraint-satisfying order: picking up the key before moving the ball forces a drop while the door is closed, and the candidate correctly traps that strategy in u5; the conjunction on u1->u2 also correctly refuses to advance when the ball was dropped back in front of the door before key pickup, and the ensuing dead end is caught by key_lost in u1. However, the candidate is rejected for one substantive coverage gap: state u3 has no key_lost transition. door_open is a condition, not a latch - the environment explicitly allows an open door to be toggled shut ('door_open ... false again if toggled shut') - and the ground-truth event is prev has_door_key true, has_door_key false now, door_open false now, which fires whenever the key is dropped while the door is currently closed, regardless of any earlier opening. From u3 an agent can toggle the shut... i.e., close the door again and then drop the key: this is exactly the forbidden 'drop the key while the door is closed' behavior and the labeler fires key_lost, but u3's else-loop absorbs it with reward 0. Since key_lost is fireable in every non-terminal, non-sink state (u0, u1, u2, u3), all four must route it to the violation sink u5 with the -0.5 penalty; the candidate covers only u0, u1, u2. Note the prose gloss 'lost before the door was opened' does not excuse this: the authoritative code semantics and the stated constraint ('the event requires the door not open') key on the current door state, so the post-opening door-re-closed regression must be enforced. Required fix: add (u3, key_lost) -> u5 to TRANSITION_FUNCTION and (u3, key_lost, u5) -> -0.5 to REWARD_FUNCTION. With that single addition the RM would be semantically complete and acceptable.

feedback: The RM is semantically faithful, safe, and well-formed. (1) Semantic fidelity: the task pairs a hard 'must not drop the key while the door is closed' constraint with the goal of picking up the box. The RM routes key_lost from every live state (u0-u3) to absorbing violation sink u5 (-0.5, no path back to u4), and reaches u4 only via the ordered chain blocker_moved -> has_door_key & blocker_moved -> door_open -> target_picked_up, matching the mechanically forced order (ball must move before the door can be toggled; key required to unlock; hands must free the key, only safely with the door open, before the box). The key-first strategy is correctly foreclosed: picking up the key in u0 leaves no else-branch reward, and the mandatory later drop fires key_lost -> u5. (2) The u1->u2 conjunction is precise: it requires simultaneous possession of the key and a cleared blocker, so a key picked up after the ball was dropped back in front yields no progress and the state correctly stays in u1; once in u2 the ball cannot regress because the agent's hands hold the key. (3) Ordered transition coverage: labels within each state are pairwise mutually exclusive per the environment's constraint list (key_lost excludes has_door_key and door_open by definition; key_lost excludes target_picked_up since drop and pick-up are distinct actions; key_lost and blocker_moved cannot coincide in u0 because blocker_moved is false throughout u0 residency and a drop step cannot also be the ball's pickup step), so the key_lost-first ordering is conflict-free and every valuation is covered; per-state else self-loops cover all irrelevant or impossible events (has_door_key alone in u0/u1, ball re-blocked, target_picked_up before u3, etc.). (4) (u3, key_lost) is live and necessary, not redundant: after unlocking, the unlocked door can be toggled shut (relocking is impossible but shutting is not), and a key drop then satisfies prev-has_door_key, not-has_door_key, not-door_open, correctly triggering the violation; door re-opening is handled by the u3 else self-loop. (5) Persistent/event distinction respected: key_lost is used strictly as a one-step event trigger, conditions as levels; no label treats key_lost as lingering. (6) Reward safety: progress is dense (0.1 at each of the three milestones) and bounded (|r| <= 1), the 1.0 terminal reward dominates (0.3 total shaping < 1.0), violation is a single -0.5 with the sink otherwise at 0, and there are no back edges, so no progress reward can be farmed by regressing and re-advancing; violation is strictly worse than completing or idling. (7) Format: exact paper headers (REWARD_MACHINE/STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES/TRANSITION_FUNCTION/REWARD_FUNCTION), predicate-only labels with '&', FINAL_STATES: u4 is nonempty, declared in STATES, and accepting for the task. Minor, non-blocking: the else self-loops (u4, else, u4) and (u5, else, u5) have no explicit reward entries (implicit 0); listing them would make the reward function total over all transitions, but omission is acceptable since they are zero by default and do not affect semantics.

feedback: All five declared propositions are implemented and no undeclared extras exist. Alignment with the documented truth conditions: `has_door_key`, `door_open`, and `target_picked_up` are verbatim matches of the reference expressions (carrying-key-with-matching-door, any open door, carrying box matching the mission string). `blocker_moved` scans the grid for the (unique) door and checks the cell at (x-1, y) for a ball; since exactly one door exists, this reduces exactly to the reference `not (ball at (dx-1, dy))`, correctly counts a carried ball as moved (it is off the grid), and correctly reverts to false if the ball is dropped back on that cell (pure grid read, condition not latch). `key_lost` is a proper event: it compares `previous_valuation['has_door_key']` (read-only access, no mutation) against the current has_door_key and door_open recomputations, is true only on the single drop step while the door is closed, and cannot co-occur with `has_door_key`, `door_open`, or `target_picked_up`. Persistent propositions read only current state; the event uses only the preceding-step snapshot. Syntax is valid Python with no imports, no actions, no side effects, and only documented API members (env.grid.get, env.width/height, env.carrying, env.mission, env.episode_memory['previous_valuation'], object type/color/is_open). Empty cells are guarded with `cell is not None`; the door is never on the boundary so x-1 is always in bounds. Constraints (door_open after blocker_moved/has_door_key, target after door_open, mutual exclusions) follow from the environment given these exact expressions.
